title: Lecture 3 — functions, domains, and symmetry
summary: A function assigns one output to every allowed input. Domain and range describe where the function starts and what it produces; graphs, the vertical-line test, and symmetry reveal the same structure geometrically.
body: Begin with the one-output rule: each $x$ in the domain determines exactly one value $f(x)$, while the range collects the outputs that occur. On a graph, this becomes the vertical-line test—any vertical line may meet a function at most once. Comparing $f(-x)$ with $f(x)$ then identifies even functions through y-axis symmetry and odd functions through origin symmetry.
